items.description: The pending-reviews block carries no untagged promise, no overdue tripwire, and no reference to a nonexistent item. python tools/pending.py --check exits 0.
steps: Run python tools/pending.py --check and python tools/pending.py; confirm the only overdue entry is 'level-layer -> flights' and record the current bullet list.

In radar.md delete the four closed bullets, each closed by the block's own rule: the flights sample-hour SHIPPED bullet, the cnh_cny maturity refresh bullet, the net_outages CLOSED bullet, and the cnh_cny reachability reference-regime bullet whose trailing line carries the phantom 'n>=250' reference.
Add the word standing to the calendar de-cycling bullet so it is marked as a standing rule.

Retag the level-layer -> flights bullet with [opened R23.1 · owner R40 · fires: date >= 2027-08-02] and retag the flights sample-hour bullet with [opened R26 · owner R40 · fires: rows_since(flights, 2026-09-02) >= 90]; retag the SOFR deferral sentence with [opened R29 · owner R40 · fires: date >= 2026-11-30].

Add one assertion to tests/lint_pending.py that every bullet paragraph in the block ends in one of three legal forms: a parseable tag with a fires predicate, the word standing, or a round-referenced closure marker.

Regenerate radar-metrics.md with python tools/episodes.py --markdown > radar-metrics.md followed by python tools/pending.py --markdown >> radar-metrics.md, then run python -m unittest discover tests -p "audit_*.py" and confirm the registry freshness test is the only remaining audit failure.
Run python tools/pending.py --check and confirm exit 0.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 1. python tools/pending.py --check exits 0 (6 tagged items, 0 overdue); python -m unittest discover tests -p "audit_*.py" leaves exactly one failure (audit_record control-line astronomy, owned by item 7 — the radar-metrics freshness failure is cleared by the regeneration); gate tier 318 passed; lint tier 56 OK; lint_no_forbidden_literal OK; replay --check 0 divergence; render_smoke OK.

items.description: tools/drift_layer.py stops crashing on a malformed obs_date and reports how many observations it skipped, so the nightly derive step completes again.
steps: Reproduce the failure: run python tools/drift_layer.py --report and record the ValueError about an invalid isoformat string.

In tools/drift_layer.py validate dates in series_for, not in walk: an empty obs_date keeps the existing fallback to the row date, a non-empty obs_date that fails a strict YYYY-MM-DD predicate drops that observation, and one shared predicate is used instead of date.fromisoformat because that function accepts basic-format dates.
Add the skip count to the tool's existing printed summary line.
Add a gate-tier test that feeds synthetic row dictionaries through the pure validation helper, using support.stub_attr for stubbing and no reads of data/.
Re-run python tools/drift_layer.py --report and python tools/drift_layer.py against the committed record and confirm exit 0.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 2. Pre-fix reproduction: python tools/drift_layer.py --report raised ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: '    <link href=...' at walk's ords parse (drift_layer.py:78). Guard added as is_strict_date (strict YYYY-MM-DD shape plus a real calendar check; date.fromisoformat alone is not the predicate because it accepts 20261022) and series_from_rows (empty obs_date keeps the row date; a non-empty bad obs_date drops the observation and is counted). series_for delegates; compute returns the skip tally; the summary line now prints '5 observation(s) dropped (unusable obs_date)' against the committed record. Three gate tests added to tests/test_level.py (red against the pre-fix module: 3 failed with AttributeError on is_strict_date/series_from_rows; green after). Both tool invocations exit 0 and data/drifts.csv re-derives byte-identically. Gates: pytest 321 passed; lint 56 OK; forbidden literal 3 OK; replay 1271 rows 0 divergent; pending 6 tagged 0 overdue; render smoke OK. Audit tier: 23 tests, 1 failure, the pre-existing control-line astronomy assertion owned by item 7 — no new failure.

items.description: core/fred.py refuses a response whose first column is not a date, so a keyless FRED error page can no longer become a reading, and the two causes in sofr_iorb_spread's unavailable note are distinguished.
steps: In core/fred.py series() require the first comma-separated field of each row to match a strict YYYY-MM-DD predicate; skip rows that fail; return None when no row survives, which the existing callers already handle as unavailable.
Add a gate-tier test that feeds the HTML fragment recorded in the incident evidence and asserts the result is None, with no network access.
In fetchers/sofr_iorb.py separate the message for one leg unavailable from the message for no shared reported date.
Run the test gate tier.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 3. Pre-fix red evidence: with core/fred.py and fetchers/sofr_iorb.py restored to HEAD, pytest on tests/test_fred_shape.py + tests/test_seedlib.py gave 5 failed, 17 passed (the HTML page parsed to ('    <link href=...Open+Sans:300', 400.0), so series() returned a reading and reading() returned raw_value 400.0 on a non-date; the sofr note said 'share no reported date' for a single dark leg and for two dark legs). Green after. series() drops any row whose first field fails a strict YYYY-MM-DD predicate ([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} plus a real calendar check, and not date.fromisoformat because 3.11+ accepts 20261022) and returns None when no row survives, which every caller already reads as unavailable; field count is not asserted, per the source-shape plan. common_pair() returns (date, a, b, missing) and latest_common() delegates, keeping its 3-tuple contract. sofr_iorb emits 'FRED <leg> unavailable' for a dark leg and 'FRED SOFR/IORB share no reported date' only for a shared-date gap. Gates: pytest 329 passed; lint 56 OK; forbidden literal 3 OK; replay 1271 rows 0 divergent; pending 6 tagged 0 overdue; render smoke OK. Audit tier: 23 tests, 1 failure, the pre-existing control-line astronomy assertion owned by item 7 — no new failure.

items.description: collect.py rejects an unusable observation date at collection time, so a malformed or future-dated obs_date becomes a stated dark row instead of a scored reading.
steps: In collect.py add a check beside the existing coerce_finite and apply_sample_guard steps: a non-empty obs_date must match a strict YYYY-MM-DD predicate and must not be later than the row's own date; on violation clear raw_value and obs_date and prefix the note with 'no reading: source returned an unusable observation date - not scored :: '.
Amend the module docstring sentence that currently declares obs_date shape validation out of scope for this contract.
Add gate-tier tests for a malformed obs_date and for an obs_date later than the row date, asserting a dark row with the stated reason.
Run the test gate tier.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 4. Pre-fix red evidence: with collect.py restored to HEAD, python -m pytest tests/test_collect_loop.py -k "UnusableObsDate or ObsDateProblem" gave 16 failed, 3 passed (AttributeError on obs_date_problem, and a malformed obs_date scored as a reading); green after. collect.py gained is_strict_date (strict [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} shape plus a real calendar check; not date.fromisoformat, which accepts 20261022) and obs_date_problem(obs_date, date); collect() darkens a row whose non-empty obs_date fails either rule with the note prefix 'no reading: source returned an unusable observation date - not scored :: '; an empty obs_date is unchanged (snapshot lines keep the collection date). The module docstring's out-of-scope sentence is replaced by the contract. A scan of every committed data/*.csv shows exactly the five known 2026-10-22 HTML obs_date rows refused and no other row affected. Gates: pytest 336 passed; lint 56 OK; forbidden literal 3 OK; replay 1271 rows 0 divergent; pending 6 tagged 0 overdue; render smoke OK. Audit tier: 23 tests, 1 failure, the pre-existing control-line astronomy assertion owned by item 7 — no new failure.

items.description: The failure alarm body states something true about a run whose collection step succeeded, and a lint test pins the new sentence.
steps: In .github/workflows/daily.yml replace only the false clause in the alarm body, keeping the schedule-expiry sentence, and add no new command substitution or backtick to the body.
Add a presence test to tests/lint_workflows.py that extracts the alarm run block through support.workflow_run_steps and asserts the new sentence, plus an absence test for the removed clause.
Run the lint tier.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 5. Pre-fix red evidence: five new lint assertions in tests/lint_workflows.py::TestFailureAlarmBodyMatchesTheStepOrder failed against HEAD's daily.yml (5 failed), each quoting the old body 'The instrument writes no row for a failed run, and the schedule itself expires after 60 days without a commit.'; green after the body edit. The alarm body now states the step order the workflow actually runs (the day is committed before the derive/render/audit steps): a run that fails before the commit step leaves the day unrecorded, a run that fails after it has already pushed the day has not lost the day and the failure lies in a later step; the schedule-expiry sentence is kept verbatim and no command substitution or backtick was added (still exactly the two pre-existing $(date -u +%F) and $(gh issue list ...), pinned by assertion). tests/lint_workflows.py also carries a behaviour-neutral type-narrowing pass over pre-existing code (the five step-index lookups and the two ci.yml job-block lookups now fail through self.fail and return a non-optional value; identical assertions and identical failure messages) to clear 10 analyzer diagnostics that were byte-identical at HEAD. Gates: pytest 336 passed; lint 61 OK (56 before, the 5 new tests); forbidden literal 3 OK; replay 1271 rows 0 divergent; pending 6 tagged 0 overdue; render smoke OK. Audit tier: 23 tests, 1 failure, the pre-existing control-line astronomy assertion owned by item 7 — no new failure.

items.description: Two prose statements that contradict the repository are corrected, one of which names the alarm issue as the day-length canary.
steps: In tests/test_control.py replace the source-redefinition identification band with wording that does not state a sign or a magnitude, since the committed offset is negative and outside the quoted band.

In radar.md correct the reference that ties the equinox false positive to issue number 3 so that it points at the Round 28 fix instead of the alarm issue, and make the same correction in tests/test_control.py.
Run the test gate tier and the lint tier.

items.description: The control-line label offset from 2026-10-22 onward is measured, dispositioned, archived and annotated, and the audit tier's astronomy assertion stops failing.
steps: Compute offline, for every committed row from 2026-10-22 onward, the residual of the recorded day length against test_control.astronomical_day_length_h for the claimed obs_date and for the following day; record the table in the annotation work.
Issue one dated request to the source for one date before 2026-10-22 and one after, and record the residual of the source value against the same model.

Apply the branch the measurement supports: a source-model change becomes a dated correction applied at the comparison site for obs_date on or after 2026-10-21, leaving astronomical_day_length_h unchanged; a label slip becomes a relabel of the affected rows to their own date plus a forward fix in the fetcher; an inconclusive measurement leaves the rows untouched and is recorded with a trigger.
Archive data/control_daylength.csv before any edit and refuse to start if the archive already exists.
Add one annotation row describing the measurement, the branch taken, and the rows touched, then make data/annotations.csv and docs/data/annotations.csv byte-equal.
Run python -m unittest discover tests -p "audit_*.py" and confirm the astronomy assertion passes.
items.regression_notes: Iteration 6. Entry red evidence: python -m unittest discover tests -p "audit_record.py" -k test_every_row_matches_the_astronomy_for_the_day_it_claims failed on the 2026-10-22 row at 0.0556 h against the 0.017 h bar; the audit tier was 23 tests, 1 failure. Measurement (offline, from the committed record): the ten rows dated 2026-10-22..2026-10-31 sit 200.3-206.5 s BELOW the first-generation model for their claimed obs_date and only +25.1..+9.1 s from the FOLLOWING day, while the four rows before them sit within 0.9 s. Source requests 2026-11-01: 2026-10-15 -> 38601 s vs 38799 s pinned on 2026-09-08 (-198 s); 2026-11-03 -> 34376 s vs 34586 s (-210 s); the source's current value for each of the ten claimed obs_dates equals the recorded value exactly, and 19 vendor samples spanning a year fit one flat effective depression (-0.84984 deg) to within 4.44 s. Branch one (published-model change), not a label slip. Fix: tests/test_control.py gained astronomical_day_length_h_v2 (pinned to those 19 vendor samples within 10 s), source_model_for + source_day_length_h (dated dispatch for obs_date >= 2026-10-21), and closest_day_margin now models all seven candidate days with the generation in force for the ROW; the shared solar-position geometry moved into a private _day_length_h verified bit-identical to the committed function over 1,200 dates from 2024-01-01, so astronomical_day_length_h keeps its numbers and its 2026-09-08 pin table. tests/audit_record.py compares against source_day_length_h. Failing test first: 6 new gate tests were red before the implementation (NameError on the new names) and green after; the margin-helper test was additionally red against the pre-fix per-candidate-day dispatch (0.0 not greater than 1.0). No committed value edited or relabelled; data/control_daylength.csv archived byte-identically as data/archive/control_daylength_pre_model_change_2026-11-01.csv (95 data rows) behind a refusal guard; one annotation row (2026-11-01, method) appended and mirrored byte-equal to docs/data/annotations.csv. Gates: pytest 342 passed (336 before, the 6 new tests); lint 61 OK; forbidden literal 3 OK; replay 1271 rows 0 divergent; pending 6 tagged 0 overdue; render smoke OK; audit tier 23 tests OK — the bundle's pre-existing control-line failure is cleared and the audit tier is now green. Independent review (reviewer, opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash) returned BLOCK on two P1s, both fixed before commit: the margin helper's per-candidate-day dispatch (code contradicting its own docstring and the annotation) and staging the archive the annotation names; four P2 prose points were taken into the annotation row.

items.description: The five 2026-10-22 FRED rows that recorded an HTML error page as a reading are archived, darkened with a stated reason, and the affected tail is re-derived so replay stays at zero divergence.
steps: Confirm the derive guard and the collection-time obs_date check are already passing, because the repair removes the rows that reproduce the crash.
Archive the five line files with a capture-named suffix and refuse to start when that archive already exists.
Rebuild each of the five 2026-10-22 rows through collect.score_row with raw_value None and a note beginning 'no reading: source returned an HTML page, not a CSV - not scored :: '.

Re-derive only rows dated 2026-10-22 or later, using published prior rows as history, and strip existing verdict notes with seedlib.strip_verdict_notes before re-scoring so verdict prose is not duplicated.
Regenerate derived outputs by running the derive command block from the daily workflow, and sync every file in collect.MIRRORED.
Add an audit-tier assertion that every committed obs_date matches a strict YYYY-MM-DD predicate.
Run python tools/replay.py --check and confirm zero divergence, then run the audit tier.

items.description: The audit tier notices a frozen derived layer: levels, stuck and leans outputs are checked against their own inputs so a silent ten-day freeze cannot recur.
steps: Add an audit assertion that the newest date in data/levels.csv equals the newest date in data/components/chokepoint_breadth.csv, evaluated only when an open state exists on that newest component date, because the level layer emits no row after a state closes.
Add recency checks for docs/data/stuck.csv and docs/data/leans.csv in the same audit file.
Run python -m unittest discover tests -p "audit_*.py" and confirm the new assertions pass against the regenerated files.

items.description: The operating contract names the seam that actually enforces the components rule, instead of a sentence that is literally false.
steps: In AGENTS.md section 4 replace the claim that the scoring path must never read components with a statement that the scoring decision, meaning score_row, normalize.judge and replay, never reads them, and that tests/test_side_channel.py binds that seam.
Run the lint tier and confirm the public-surface and side-channel tests still pass.
